title: From the Cape to Canton: The Dutch Indian Ocean World, 1600–1800 — A Littoral Census
container: Journal of Indian Ocean World Studies
note: Read via open-access PDF (text fetched, tables 1–2 on pp. 35–37). Gives settlement-level European counts for Batavia, Ternate, Makassar, Ambon, Banda, Malacca. No DOI or issue number appears in the PDF; none recorded. Keeps 'Europeans' and 'mixed peoples' as separate columns, but never defines 'European'.

title: The Social World of Batavia: Europeans and Eurasians in Colonial Indonesia (2nd ed.; 1st ed. 1983)
note: Verified on the Project MUSE record (publisher, 2nd edition 2009, ISBN, 312 pp., description). Book itself NOT read; used only for its stated argument (Batavia as a mixed Indo-Dutch society). No page numbers claimed.

title: Education at home: the age-specific pattern of migration between the Netherlands and the former Dutch East Indies around 1930
note: Read via open-access PDF (text fetched). Gives about 170,000 Europeans in 1920 and 240,000 in 1930 (p. 339), the legal-category discussion (pp. 336, 341, 345) and about 2,000 Europeans on Java and Madura in 1814 excluding military (p. 338).

title: A demographic history of the Indo-Dutch population, 1930–2001
note: Read via the NIDI author-copy PDF (jpr-21-01-vanimhoff.pdf; abstract on p. 47; tables to p. 68). Pages cited are as printed in that copy. End page and DOI not verified (a search result linked doi 10.1007/BF03032210 but the title was not confirmed, so no DOI is recorded). Note: this article gives 246,000 Europeans in 1930 (p. 53), slightly above the census table figure.

title: Post-Colonial Immigrants and Identity Formations in the Netherlands
note: Open access on OAPEN (DOI and 252 pp. verified on the OAPEN record; ISBN from the AUP product URL). Text read via the OAPEN PDF. Pages are those printed in the PDF; the fetch tool reports that Jones's chapter 2 pages are inferred from running headers, so treat p. 32–33, 37, 45 as approximate. Introduction by Bosma, ch. 2 by Guno Jones, ch. 3 by Laarman.

title: Women and the Colonial State: Essays on Gender and Modernity in the Netherlands Indies, 1900–1942
note: Open-access PDF on OAPEN (title, publisher, year as reported by the PDF text). Introduction ('Historical Context') quotes 240,000 Europeans in 1930, 80% on Java, 471 to 884 women per 1,000 men (1880–1930), citing Volkstelling 1930 vol. VI. The OAPEN text has no printed page numbers in the introduction; no pages claimed. A later passage (p. 86 as printed in the PDF) discusses 'totokisation' and four-fifths on Java; the chapter containing it was not identified. Subtitle and ISBN not verified.

authors: Beets, Gijs; Huisman, Corina; Van Imhoff, Evert; Koesoebjono, Santo; Walhout, Evelien
title: De demografische geschiedenis van de Indische Nederlanders (NIDI Rapport 64)
container: Nederlands Interdisciplinair Demografisch Instituut (NIDI), Den Haag
note: Research-institute report in Dutch (read via PDF text, with translation by the fetch tool; Ejak does not read Dutch, so quotations are paraphrased in English). Table 3.1 gives 240,417 Europeans in the 1930 census (p. 25). Pages as printed.

authors: NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies
title: The Japanese Occupation and Pacific War (in numbers)
container: NIOD (institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences), FAQ page
note: Research-institute page compiling De Jong, Zwitzer, Van Velden, Daws and Meijer. Date of page not stated. Gives POW and civilian-internee counts, death ranges and the 120,000–200,000 outside camps. No pages.

title: The Ethnic Profile of Djakarta
note: Cornell Modern Indonesia Project journal; read via Cornell eCommons PDF. Table III (p. 166) gives 1930 census Europeans in Batavia–Meester Cornelis (37,076), citing Volkstelling 1930 vol. VI p. 264. Journal's refereeing in 1967 not verified, so peer_reviewed is left false; article is by a university scholar and works from the census.

title: Planter and Peasant: Colonial Policy and the Agrarian Struggle in East Sumatra, 1863–1947
container: Verhandelingen van het Koninklijk Instituut voor Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 84, Martinus Nijhoff
note: KITLV research-institute monograph, open access on OAPEN; read in part (pp. 14, 35–36, 63, 87, 91). Table 6, p. 63: about 11 thousand Europeans in East Sumatra in 1930, 0.7% of 1,498 thousand.

title: Indonesisch geweld tegen de burgerbevolking in West-Java, 1945–1949. Een verkenning
note: Dutch-language article in Leiden's history journal (read via the repository PDF, translated by the fetch tool). p. 61: 25,000–30,000 Dutch and Indo-European civilian casualties, about 10%, citing W.H. Frederick 2012, p. 369 (Frederick not checked). Peer-review status of Leidschrift not verified.

title: Het geluid van geweld: Bersiap en de dynamiek van geweld tijdens de eerste fase van de Indonesische revolutie, 1945–1946
note: Dutch-language open-access monograph. Read only pp. ~1–25 and ~100–123 (local incidents and the 398-camp figure, p. 118). Chapter 8 (victim estimates) was NOT read. Peer-review status not verified.

title: Equal Despite Different Entitlements? M.C. Piepers' Ambiguous Conceptualization of Legal Equality (1898)
container: SASDAYA: Gadjah Mada Journal of Humanities
note: Read via open-access PDF text. p. 120: article 109 of the 1854 regeringsreglement; Japanese received European legal status in 1899. pp. 124–126: individual equation to Europeans.

title: Civilization, Law, and Race: The Drafting Process of the 'Japanese Law' and the Debate over Civilization
note: Abstract only on J-STAGE: after the 1896 navigation treaty the Netherlands raised Japanese in the Indies from 'inlander' to quasi-European status. The abstract does not give the 1899 date (taken from Linde & Legêne 2024).

title: Review of Bosma & Raben, Being 'Dutch' in the Indies
note: Book review (Cornell eCommons PDF). p. 187: 240,000 Europeans in 1930, Japanese 7,195, Armenians 542, about 9,000 'Staatsblad Europeans'; p. 190: authors' claim that Indos were almost 80% of the European population, with the reviewer noting it counts creoles. Used for these secondary reports of Bosma & Raben, whose book was not read.

title: Van vreemdeling naar vaderlander: De invloed van maatschappelijke organisaties in het repatrianten- en spijtoptantendebat 1950–1963
container: Research Master thesis (30 EC), Leiden University; supervisor M.L.J.C. Schrover
note: Dutch-language Leiden research-master thesis. p. 24: 5 December 1957 (Zwarte Sinterklaas), Dutch declared a danger to the state, firms nationalised; spijtoptanten defined. p. 25: about 13,000 spijtoptanten left within two years of the 1960 policy shift; 1,599 visas in 1959–60. Gives no count for 1957–58 departures.

title: The United Nations, West Papua and the Act of Free Choice: de-colonisation in action?
container: Papers presented at the seminar on West New Guinea (KNAW / Huygens ING resource)
note: Seminar paper hosted by Huygens ING (KNAW). Dates: New York Agreement August 1962; UNTEA took over 1 October 1962; transfer to Indonesia 1 May 1963. Paper runs pp. 60–71 in the volume; year and volume title not stated in the text I could read.

title: Volkstelling 1930, deel VI: Europeanen in Nederlandsch-Indië
note: Colonial government census, cited here ONLY as reported by NIDI 2002 (Table 3.1, p. 25), Castles 1967 (p. 166, citing vol. VI p. 264) and Locher-Scholten 2000. The volume itself was not opened; publisher and printing year were not verified. A catalogue record exists (CiNii: 'Europeanen in Nederlandsch-Indië') but was not opened.
